clue.text: Extremely rare broadcast of Irish writer's triumph

indicators.note: extremely points to the extremes of the word, its two end letters only
something broadcast is heard rather than seen, so the name is taken by its sound

blocks.note: the first and last letters of rare
James Joyce, the Irish novelist; his name said aloud is spelt a different way here

explanation.surface: A rare radio programme celebrates the achievement of an Irish author.
explanation.walkthrough: The spelling JOICE is chosen to fit the answer, since only the sound of Joyce counts. The 's joins wordplay to definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To rejoice is to exult or celebrate, which is what to triumph means as a verb.

clue.text: Boat dispatched to save swimmer somewhere in Africa

indicators.note: something dispatched is sent off or done away with, so these letters are knocked out of order
to save something is to keep it safe inside, so one piece goes within the other

blocks.note: the letters of boat rearranged
a swan is a bird that swims

explanation.surface: A boat is sent out to rescue someone in difficulty in the water off Africa.
explanation.definitionFit: Botswana is a landlocked country in southern Africa, so it is one place on that continent.

clue.text: Mutilated head on stick

indicators.note: something mutilated is badly damaged and misshapen, so the letters are mangled into a new order

blocks.note: the letters of head rearranged
re means on or about, as in a letter heading

explanation.surface: A grisly image of a severed head displayed on a pole.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stick' looks like the noun the head is placed on, but it is the verb defining the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To adhere is to cling fast to a surface, the same as to stick.

clue.text: Rattle steel nut loose

indicators.note: letters set loose are freed from their fixed places and can fall into another order

blocks.note: taken as written for rearranging

explanation.surface: A metal nut has worked loose and is rattling about.
explanation.definitionFit: To rattle someone is to disturb their composure, which is to unsettle them.

clue.text: Swear about loud football hooligans

blocks.note: a is an abbreviation for about
f, forte, is the musical marking for loud
a firm is slang for an organised gang of football hooligans

explanation.surface: Rowdy football fans shout and curse loudly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Swear' suggests bad language from the terraces, but it means to declare under oath. In British slang a firm is a hooligan gang attached to a football club.
explanation.definitionFit: To affirm is to state solemnly as true, the formal sense of swearing to something.

clue.text: Spot book on language with preface missing

indicators.note: a preface comes at the front, so the word loses its opening letter

blocks.note: B is the standard abbreviation for book
Flemish is the Dutch spoken in Belgium

explanation.surface: Locate a book about a language whose introduction has gone.
explanation.definitionFit: A blemish is a small mark or flaw on a surface, such as a spot on the skin.

clue.text: Enemy's cover protected by spy on the other side

indicators.note: a cover wraps the outside, so only the outer letters of the word are kept
what is protected sits inside its guard, so these letters go within another word

blocks.note: James Bond, the fictional spy
the first and last letters of enemy

explanation.surface: An enemy agent's cover story is being shielded by a spy working for the opposite camp.
explanation.definitionFit: Beyond describes what lies past a boundary, so on its far or other side.

clue.text: Wife to go down after hot date – that's a bonus

indicators.note: after places one piece behind the others in the order of the answer

blocks.note: W is the abbreviation for wife
in means fashionable, the slang sense of hot
D is the abbreviation for date
to fall is to go down

explanation.surface: A wife has a romantic tryst with an attractive partner, then trips over.
explanation.definitionFit: A windfall is an unexpected gain of money, a bonus that arrives unearned.

clue.text: Present coverage featured in 7A, 8A, 12A, 13A, 1D, 14D, 15D, 16D and 21D

blocks.note: surface reading: reporting of current events, as a newspaper gives
setter's reading: what covers a present, that is a gift
thematic padding pointing to the entries that carry the theme; it gives no letters

explanation.surface: Topical news coverage appears across a list of the puzzle's answers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Present' reads as 'current' but means a gift. The rest of the clue just lists the puzzle's themed entries.
explanation.definitionFit: Wrapping paper is the decorated sheet used to cover a gift before giving it.

clue.text: Giant, athletic climber

blocks.note: a monster is a giant of a thing
A is short for athletic, as in the baseball team the Oakland A's, the Athletics

explanation.surface: A huge, sporty mountaineer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Climber' suggests a mountaineer, but it is a plant.
explanation.definitionFit: Monstera is a genus of tropical vines, including the Swiss cheese plant, that climb trees in the wild.

clue.text: Imagine not having an Independent cryptic puzzle!

indicators.note: not having something means going without it, so that letter is dropped
cryptic means obscure or mysterious, so the remaining letters are disguised in a new order

blocks.note: taken as written
I is the abbreviation for Independent

explanation.surface: Picture life without the Independent's daily cryptic crossword!
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads 'an Independent cryptic puzzle' as one phrase, but 'cryptic' belongs to the wordplay and 'puzzle' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: An enigma is a riddle or mystery, something baffling to work out, so a puzzle.

clue.text: Pull it together to dump fiancée at last during drink

indicators.note: at last points to the final letter of the word before it
something happening during another thing falls within it, so these letters go inside

blocks.note: to sup is to drink
crap is slang for a dump, rubbish
the final letter of fiancée

explanation.surface: Someone must steel themselves over a drink to break off an engagement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dump' looks like a verb about the fiancée, but it is a noun meaning rubbish.
explanation.definitionFit: To scrape up is to gather or collect something with difficulty, bringing it together bit by bit.

clue.text: Most boring cricket match involving Durham's tail-enders

indicators.note: the tail-enders are those at the very end, so only the closing letters of the word are kept
to involve something is to take it in, so the letters go inside another word

blocks.note: a Test is an international cricket match
the last two letters of Durham

explanation.surface: A dull cricket match in which Durham's lower-order batsmen played.
explanation.walkthrough: Durham is an English county cricket team; in cricket the tail-enders are the weak batsmen who come in last.
explanation.definitionFit: Tamest is the superlative of tame, meaning dull or lacking excitement, so most boring.

clue.text: Wilde's second poem written in friend's house

indicators.note: second points to the letter in position two of the name
something written in another is set inside it, so these letters go within

blocks.note: a mate is a friend
the second letter of Wilde
a sonnet is a fourteen-line poem

explanation.surface: Oscar Wilde's latest verse composed at a friend's home.
explanation.definitionFit: A maisonette is a flat on two floors with its own entrance, a kind of dwelling or house.

clue.text: Way for American to act crabby?

blocks.note: first meaning: the American term for a pavement
second meaning: to move sideways like a crab, split as two words

explanation.walkthrough: 'Crabby' suggests bad temper, but here it means behaving like a crab, which scuttles sideways.
explanation.definitionFit: In US English a sidewalk is the footpath beside a road, and a crab famously walks sideways.

clue.text: Perhaps Dennis bores by going on and on

indicators.note: to bore is to drill into something, so this piece goes inside the next

blocks.note: times means by, as in multiplication
Les Dennis is a British comedian and game-show host, so Dennis is a surname that could follow it

explanation.surface: Someone called Dennis is tiresome because he keeps talking endlessly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bores' looks like a noun or verb for tedium, but it means drills into. 'Perhaps' signals that Dennis is the surname of a Les.
explanation.definitionFit: Something timeless is not limited by time, so it lasts for ever, going on and on.

clue.text: Get hard cuddling Rosemary? "Sweetie!"

indicators.note: to cuddle is to hold close in one's arms, so one word wraps round the other

blocks.note: to set is to become solid
rosemary is an example of a herb, hence the question mark

explanation.surface: Someone getting aroused while hugging a woman called Rosemary and calling her darling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sweetie' reads as a term of endearment, but in Britain a sweetie is a sweet, a piece of candy.
explanation.definitionFit: Sherbet is a fizzy powdered confectionery sold in British sweet shops, so it is a sweet.

clue.text: Don't stop parking sensor going off

indicators.note: something going off has gone bad or exploded, so these letters are disturbed into a new order

blocks.note: P is the road-sign abbreviation for parking
the letters of sensor rearranged

explanation.surface: A driver is urged to keep going while the car's parking sensor beeps.
explanation.definitionFit: To press on is to continue in spite of difficulty, which is to keep going and not stop.

clue.text: Mum shot dead in the shadows

indicators.note: something shot is ruined or broken, so these letters are knocked into a new order

blocks.note: mum means silent, and sh is the call for silence
the letters of dead rearranged

explanation.surface: A mother is gunned down in a dark place, like a crime-novel scene.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mum' reads as mother but means quiet, as in keeping mum.
explanation.definitionFit: Something shaded is kept out of the light, so it lies in the shadows.

clue.text: Youngster put up with crap Fiat

indicators.note: in a down answer something put up is raised, so the word reads from bottom to top

blocks.note: a kid is a child
tat is cheap rubbish

explanation.surface: A child had to tolerate a rubbish Fiat car.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fiat' reads as the Italian car maker, but it is a decree; 'put up with' is split, 'put up' reversing and 'with' joining.
explanation.definitionFit: A diktat is an order imposed by authority without consultation, which is what a fiat is.

clue.text: Frank or Luke's place?

blocks.note: first meaning: a frank is the mark stamped on mail
second meaning: the Gospel of Luke comes after, or post, the Gospel of Mark

explanation.walkthrough: 'Frank' and 'Luke' look like two men's names, but Frank is a mail mark and Luke a Gospel, placed straight after Mark in the Bible.
explanation.definitionFit: A postmark is the official stamp franking a letter, and Luke's Gospel follows Mark's in the New Testament.

clue.text: Some nudist ran down beach

indicators.note: some means only part of what follows, so the letters sit inside the phrase

blocks.note: found across the three words

explanation.surface: A naturist runs down to the seaside.
explanation.definitionFit: Strand is a literary word for a shore or beach, as in being stranded.

clue.text: Two vessels travelling west in city

indicators.note: in an across answer west is leftward, so the letters run from right to left

blocks.note: a wok is a cooking vessel and an ark a sailing one

explanation.surface: A pair of ships heading west towards a city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Vessels' suggests ships for both, but one is a pan.
explanation.definitionFit: Krakow is a historic city in southern Poland, its former royal capital.

clue.text: Exercise securing high salary freeze

indicators.note: high means intoxicated, so the letters are in a muddled state
to secure something is to hold it fast within, so one piece encloses the other

blocks.note: PE is physical education, exercise at school
the letters of salary rearranged

explanation.surface: A workout routine that guarantees a big pay packet, followed by a pay freeze.
explanation.walkthrough: 'High salary freeze' reads as one phrase, but 'high' belongs to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: To paralyse is to make unable to move, just as fear can freeze someone.

clue.text: First to review online follower's business

indicators.note: first points to the opening letter of the word that follows

blocks.note: the opening letter of review
e, as in e-mail, means online or electronic
one who tails another follows them

explanation.surface: Someone checks out an internet fan's company.
explanation.definitionFit: A retailer is a shop or firm selling goods to the public, so a kind of business.

clue.text: She doesn't appear to eat contents of bowl

indicators.note: the contents are what lie inside, so only the inner letters are kept, the outer ones dropped

blocks.note: to nosh is to eat, informally
the inner letters of bowl

explanation.surface: A woman skips a meal and does not show up to eat what is in her bowl.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is a whole phrase: 'She' is any person who fails to turn up.
explanation.definitionFit: A no-show is a person who books or is expected but fails to turn up.
